title: Anchored version selection and client behavior for model refs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define a single, minimally surprising semantics surface for 'anchored' model refs in the Redwood API and SDKs. This ticket captures requirements and the proposed runtime/client behaviour when callers specify model selectors using tag names, semver ranges, and commit hashes. Goal: make pins deterministic, safe for rollouts, and easy to audit while allowing graceful fallbacks under capacity or compatibility constraints.
background: We onboard open and internal models that can be referenced via tags (stable, canary), semver-like release versions, or commit hashes (full reproducibility). Currently SDK callers and runtime have ad-hoc resolution behavior; different clients interpret unspecified parts differently. This causes surprising rollouts and debugging overhead for customers using Dedicated/Private deployments. We need a consistent contract across REST API and official SDKs that balances reproducibility, safe upgrades, and operational flexibility.
proposal: Introduce an 'anchored' model-ref resolution contract and SDK helpers:
proposal_points: 1) Anchor types: callers may pass one of: tag:<name>, semver:<range>, hash:<commit>, or plain <model-name> (unanchored).

2) Deterministic precedence: resolution preference is hash -> exact semver equality -> semver range (highest satisfying) -> tag (explicit tag mapping to current release) -> unanchored latest-compatible. Runtime will document this order and expose telemetry when falls happen.

3) Profile-compatibility check: when resolving to a candidate binary, runtime verifies that the model's published performance profile (throughput/latency/kv/cache-size) is compatible with the client's requested constraints (max-latency-ms, min-throughput). If incompatible, resolution either falls back according to policy or returns 412 with a clear message.

4) SDK opt-in strict mode: SDKs provide 'anchoredStrict: true' which enforces that resolution must match the explicit anchor type (e.g., semver range must not resolve to a tag mapping) or fail fast, preventing silent upgrades.

5) Fallback policy: default fallback sequence for hosted runtime is: try primary resolution -> if capacity rejection or incompatibility then try pinned-compatible variants (quantized/reduced-kv variants) -> if still unavailable and caller provided 'allowFallback=true' then resolve to majority-stable fallback model; else return explicit error with suggested alternatives.

6) Telemetry/trace: emit resolution trace (candidate list, selected candidate, reason for fallback) per request when 'X-Enable-Resolution-Trace' header is set. Persist aggregated counts into Console per model-ref.
7) Auditability: resolved artifact must include the resolved identifier (full commit hash) in every response, plus a server-side 'resolution_id' in logs for tracing.
8) Migration path: maintain current default runtime for unanchored refs; new behavior gated behind 'anchored' feature flag for a single release window to let customers opt-in and validate.
acceptance_criteria: API: /models/resolve accepts anchors and returns candidate list and resolved commit in JSON. Example response includes 'resolved_commit' and 'resolution_trace'.
SDKs: JS and Python SDKs expose ModelRef helpers and an 'anchoredStrict' flag. Unit and integration tests validate resolution order and fallback behavior.
Console: new model-ref resolution telemetry page that shows fallback counts and distribution of resolved commits for a given public ref.
Runtime: profile-compatibility check implemented and tested for at least two incompatibility modes (latency and kv-memory).
Docs: PRD and SDK docs updated with examples and migration guide.
api_contract_examples: SDK (JS) example: const ref = ModelRef.parse('image-dist@tag:stable'); await client.infer({model: ref, anchoredStrict: true}); // throws if resolution doesn't match explicit tag mapping
migration_notes: Default behaviour unchanged for unanchored refs until feature-flag window ends.
Provide a console toggle 'Reveal resolved commit' for accounts to verify before flipping anchors to strict mode.
Outreach: email top 50 customers using pinned tags with recommended 'anchoredStrict' test plan.
Deprecation: old ad-hoc resolution endpoints will be marked deprecated in 90 days after GA and removed 180 days after GA.
compatibility_and_backwards_compatibilit: Existing callers that pass plain model names see no change until opt-in.
If SDKs set anchoredStrict=false (default), runtime may still perform fallbacks but will include resolution_trace. This allows passive verification.
Commits referenced by hash are always authoritative; if a customer used an alias that previously resolved to a different commit, their anchoredStrict call will surface mismatch so they can adjust.
open_questions: Should we add a soft TTL for tag mappings (e.g., tags are sticky for 24h after assignment) to prevent flapping?
How should Dedicated/private control planes receive new profile compatibility rules? Push via manifest or pull from service?
Do we need an explicit 'deny-list' for automatic fallback to very-low-accuracy variants?
